turns.content: I just found out Julian was passed over for the promotion. He worked three years for that. We're on day 28 of the 30-day pause. Our sit-down is Friday. I want to send him a brief message right now—just "I heard, I'm sorry, I'm here." No expectations. Is that a bad idea?
This is continuing the pause with Julian, so I’m pulling the relevant prior context before I weigh in. I’ll keep it tight and practical.

You're saying wait until Friday. But Julian explicitly asked for space, not for silence during a crisis. There's a difference between respecting a boundary and abandoning someone when they've been crushed. I've watched Esther Perel's lectures on this—she's clear that rigid rule-keeping during genuine trauma can be more damaging than the breach. My own counselor agrees: offering unconditional support when someone is grieving builds trust, it doesn't break it. So I need you to answer this directly—do you really believe withholding kindness right now is the healthier choice for our marriage?
